dimension.category_description: How users inspect, modify, scope, revise, accept, program, or interrupt generated work at the artifact level.
dimension.classification_boundary: Centers user control during or after generation, including editable intermediate generators and representations.

patterns.short_summary: The system pre-populates the working artifact with generated content that occupies its final position, and the user's task begins from that filled state.
A continuous artifact is partitioned into named units, and each unit becomes an independently addressable object.
The system opens with a concrete proposal rather than an empty field; the user reacts to it; the reaction becomes an input that yields a revised version of the same artifact.
The user designates a sub-extent of the artifact and the generative operation applies to exactly that extent.
The model's output is not the artifact the user wanted but a generator of it: code, a hierarchical program, or a parameterized template that must be executed or instantiated to yield the artifact.

A finished artifact that the system did not produce is decomposed back into an underlying structure — data table, encoding spec, component graph, layered representation — and that recovered structure becomes the object the user manipulates.
Two or more views of the same underlying object are shown at once, each of them editable, and an edit in any one propagates to the others.
Alongside the generative route, the interface keeps a route by which the user authors the same material directly: a free-text field, editable nodes, a custom operation, a user-added prompt.
Every system-produced item arrives with the same small, closed set of actions attached to it, so the user's response to any suggestion is drawn from a uniform vocabulary.
A process that would otherwise run to completion is made interruptible: the user can halt it, change its parameters while it continues, or leave it before it ends.
